bullets.title: NVDA backstops $250B OpenAI data center; $500B SK Group AI partnership
bullets.body: WSJ broke that NVDA is in talks to provide a ~$250B financial backstop for OpenAI's Ohio 10-GW data center (built by SoftBank's energy unit). Separately, NVDA and SK Group announced a $500B+ initiative spanning AI factories and next-generation memory (SK Telecom building 2 GW NVDA Vera Rubin DSX factory; SK Hynix co-developing next-gen memory). NVDA also launched an AI Technology Center at Seoul National University and committed $1B alongside Brookfield's $9B for Naver's Korea AI factory.

bullets.title: NVDA evolving into AI infrastructure financier—bullish demand, new credit risk
bullets.body: Fintwit noted NVDA is transitioning from a chip supplier to a financier/credit backer of AI infrastructure, potentially securing enormous long-term GPU demand but also introducing customer credit-risk and 'circular dynamics' concerns. NVDA is now using Vera CPUs to design its next-gen chips, and is the largest open-source contributor to Hugging Face.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex at $550B+ in 2026; GOOGL, AMZN, META all raising outlooks
bullets.body: Alphabet raised its 2026 capex outlook to $195B–$205B, Amazon expects ~$200B, and Meta plans $125B–$145B, bringing the three-company combined potential to ~$550B. GOOGL's order backlog has surged to $500B from ~$100B a year ago. Goldman's trading desk flagged tech as 'sold on the news' while GOOGL FCF briefly turned negative for the first time ever on the capex revelation.

bullets.title: AAPL vs MU: Apple lobbies to use Chinese memory chips abroad; Micron opposes
bullets.body: WSJ reported Apple is seeking White House approval to source Chinese-made DRAM for overseas products, while Micron's CEO Sanjay Mehrotra has actively lobbied Commerce Secretary Lutnick against the move. AAPL is up ~22% in July (its best monthly Nasdaq outperformance in 20 years) while DDR5 32GB RAM prices have surged ~620% since September 2025, squeezing MacBook margins.

bullets.title: INTC server CPU ASPs up 48% in 10-Q; SK Hynix Ohio deal confirmed
bullets.body: Multiple accounts highlighted an Intel 10-Q detail showing server CPU average selling prices up 48%, signaling pricing power recovery. Ohio Senator Jon Husted separately confirmed Intel's deal with SK Hynix for Ohio chip plants. Intel also announced a €5B capital investment at its Leixlip Ireland campus for AI and HPC. However, INTC reversed a 10% after-hours gain to close down 7%—a 17% intraday whipsaw attributed to algos.

bullets.title: AVGO wins $200B Samsung MOU for advanced memory and foundry through 2030
bullets.body: Samsung and Broadcom signed a memorandum of understanding covering more than $200B of cooperation through 2030, spanning advanced memory semiconductor supply and foundry services including Samsung's 2nm-and-below processes. AVGO named alongside AMD and MSFT in a 30-day partnership recap showing Samsung ($200B+ MOU), AMD/Cerebras AI memory collaboration, and SK Group ($500B+ LOI with NVDA).

bullets.title: MU: CXMT IPO surges 465%—near-term DRAM relief but long-term oversupply risk
bullets.body: Chinese memory maker CXMT debuted up ~470% in Shanghai, surpassing Intel's market cap and reaching $85B. Fintwit noted CXMT's HBM production is captive to Huawei, leaving MU in a different market position. A Micron/Meta joint white paper documented a 38x performance slowdown when shuffle data spills from DRAM to SSD, underscoring DRAM's irreplaceable role. Michael Burry added to short positions in both MU and NVDA.

bullets.title: TSLA plunges 18% in worst week since 2022; options show $11.4M deep put sweep
bullets.body: Tesla dropped ~18% on the week after reporting Q2 2026 earnings—its worst weekly decline since 2022 and erasing ~$500B in market cap from the December highs. Energy storage revenue per KWh fell 20% YoY to a record-low $232.5, with Tesla's CFO flagging intense global battery competition. An $11.4M deep ITM put sweep was flagged as signaling significant bearish conviction. A long-time Tesla analyst lamented the investor community as 'hollowed out and corrupted by opportunists.'

bullets.title: GOOGL: Chamath bullish at 32% ROIC history; Waymo explores Uber split
bullets.body: Chamath called GOOGL a 'compounding machine' with a 32% average ROIC since IPO and capable of winning the entire AI stack, dismissing the ~7% stock drop on capex guidance. Separately, FT reported Waymo is exploring options to exit its partnership with Uber, which could reshape both companies' autonomous vehicle strategies.

bullets.title: MSFT at decade-low 21x earnings per Ackman; Pershing Square holds $1.98B UBER
bullets.body: Bill Ackman flagged MSFT as trading at its lowest earnings multiple in at least a decade (~21x), calling it historically cheap. Ackman separately said consumers will 'still open the Uber app' prioritizing cheapest/fastest transport, with Pershing Square holding $1.98B in UBER. MSFT is down ~31% from its all-time high while UBER hit new 52-week lows this week.

bullets.title: TSMC 2nm hits 20K wafer/month at Fab 20; NVDA GB300 'Made in USA' milestone
bullets.body: TSMC's first 2nm fab (Fab 20, Hsinchu) reached 20,000 wafers per month—the highest output among the five Taiwan 2nm fabs ramping. Nvidia's GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra 4nm chips began rolling off the line at TSMC Arizona, with CoWoS packaging the final step for full US localization. Taiwan's semiconductor sector power demand is projected to jump 54% to 80B kWh by 2030.

bullets.title: AMD: Vultr deploys EPYC/Instinct across 33 regions; Zen 6/7 roadmap details
bullets.body: Cloud provider Vultr is building its AI public cloud across 33 global regions using AMD EPYC CPUs and Instinct GPUs, validating AMD's price-performance positioning. Separately, EPYC Venice previewed Zen 6 features (more cores, cache, clock), while Zen 7 may be the last AM5 Ryzen generation before Zen 8 moves to AM6 with DDR6/PCIe 6.0.

bullets.title: SNDK: Bearish NAND rumors circulate; SanDisk LTA with Meta at below-market pricing
bullets.body: Multiple accounts flagged bearish notes and rumors on NAND, particularly from China, tied to QLC price negotiations. SanDisk reportedly signed a long-term agreement with Meta at below-market pricing. TrendForce NAND oversupply conditions are being cited alongside concerns about whether the memory supply/demand thesis can hold beyond one year.

bullets.title: Oil drops 4–5% as US-Iran strike pause; geopolitical risk structure explained
bullets.body: US halted Iran strikes for two consecutive nights (Oman mediated talks), sending Brent down ~5% to ~$92 and S&P 500 futures up 0.6% / Nasdaq futures +1.4%. Polymarket priced 55–72% odds of a ceasefire by August 31. JPM noted each additional month of Iran conflict adds $7–8/bbl to Brent; simultaneous Hormuz/Red Sea closure could push crude to $124/bbl. US Strategic Petroleum Reserve at lowest level since March 1983.

bullets.title: Bond market repricing: Fed hike odds surge; global yields at 2008 highs
bullets.body: Bond market swung from pricing 2 Fed cuts at year start to 1–2 hikes today. Polymarket showed 17–36% odds of a hike this week. Global bond yields hit highest since the 2008 financial crisis. US investment-grade bond funds saw a record $7.1B weekly outflow. US margin debt hit a record $1.5T in June (+49% YoY), and S&P 500 short interest rose to ~3.7% of free float—near a 15-year high.

bullets.title: S&P 500 Q2 earnings blowout: 38% YoY growth, record 15.7% net margin
bullets.body: With 27% of S&P 500 companies having reported, blended Q2 EPS growth stands at 37.9% YoY—on pace for the strongest quarter since Q3 2021—and 86% of reporters beat EPS estimates. Net profit margin projected at a record 15.7%. Semiconductors account for nearly half of S&P 500 earnings growth. Nasdaq 100 is simultaneously down 7% in July, tracking its worst July since 2004.

bullets.title: ORCL CDS hits record wides; investors drawing line on AI capex discipline
bullets.body: Oracle CDS widened to record levels amid broader hyperscaler credit deterioration. Multiple accounts noted Apple's disciplined AI spending rewarded (+56% YoY) vs. Oracle's overspending punished (–52% YoY; down 67% from September ATH). ORCL cited as an example of counterparty risk when AI infrastructure capacity commitments exceed revenue realization.

bullets.title: GLW bullish as data-center connectivity infrastructure AI play
bullets.body: One fintwit analyst called GLW 'strongly bullish' as a data-center connectivity infrastructure company with inside DCI and optical fiber exposure to AI infrastructure. NVDA's CPO test bottleneck analysis named seven companies owning the 4-stage test process; FormFactor Q1 2026 shows NVDA at 10.2% of revenue, suggesting CPO ramp is real.

bullets.title: AAPL massive outperformance: +22% vs Nasdaq in July; memory supply shift
bullets.body: Apple outperformed the Nasdaq by 22 percentage points in July—the largest monthly outperformance in 20 years. Fintwit attributed this partly to memory suppliers 'rebelling': AI demand shifted pricing power away from Apple's historical LPDDR dominance. AAPL also posted $129B in free cash flow over the past year. Privacy positioning for Apple smart glasses flagged as a potential differentiator.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: Paramount freezes merger amid state AG lawsuits; trial in 2027
bullets.body: Paramount agreed to delay closing the Warner Bros Discovery transaction until summer 2027, bypassing an injunction hearing and proceeding directly to trial. Multiple analysts noted Paramount broke its 'close this summer' promise to Wall Street. LightShed's Greenfield said Paramount 'may have to make structural alterations' to close the deal.
